Fraud Detection Platform Architecture

The MFS Fraud Detection platform is a real-time ML-powered system that scores every incoming transaction for fraud probability within 50ms SLA.

System Components

  • Feature Extraction Service: Consumes raw transactions from Kafka topic mfs.txn.raw, computes real-time features (velocity, merchant risk, device fingerprint, geolocation anomaly), and publishes enriched events to mfs.txn.features. Runs on mfs-fraud-pod-01 under svc-fraud-engine service account.
  • Fraud Scoring Engine: XGBoost model (v2, ONNX format) served via gRPC. Deployed across mfs-fraud-pod-01 and mfs-fraud-pod-02 in mfs-prod OpenShift namespace for high availability.
  • Model Registry: MLflow-based model versioning with A/B testing support. Metadata stored in mfs_fraud_db.model_registry on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal.

Data Flow

Transaction Ingestion → Feature Extraction → Fraud Scoring → Decision (approve/review/decline) → Alert Generation

Related Work Items

FRD-100 (Feature), FRD-101 (Model Pipeline), FRD-102 (Feature Extraction), FRD-103 (Model Versioning)

Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Framework

The AML compliance engine implements FinCEN regulatory requirements for detecting and reporting suspicious financial activity.

Detection Patterns

PatternDescriptionRule ID
StructuringTransactions split to stay below $10,000 CTR thresholdAML-STRUCT-001
LayeringRapid inter-account fund movements to obscure originAML-LAYER-001
IntegrationIllicit funds merged into legitimate-appearing transactionsAML-INTEG-001

Reporting Automation

SAR forms auto-populated from case data via FRD-311. CTR auto-filing for >$10K transactions via FRD-321. Integration with FinCEN BSA E-Filing system.

Infrastructure

AML engine runs on mfs-aml-pod-01 in mfs-prod namespace under svc-aml-engine. Data stored in mfs_aml_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal.

Related

EPC-203 (Epic), FRD-300 (Feature), FRD-301 (Rule Engine), FRD-302 (SAR Automation)

Real-time Transaction Monitoring System Design

The transaction monitoring system provides continuous surveillance of financial transactions using velocity-based rules and statistical anomaly detection.

Velocity Monitoring

Tracks transaction rates across three dimensions:

  • Per-account: Flags accounts exceeding normal transaction frequency
  • Per-merchant: Identifies merchants with unusual inbound transaction patterns
  • Per-device: Detects device-based fraud rings

Time windows: 1 minute, 5 minutes, 1 hour, 24 hours. Thresholds configurable via YAML rules with hot-reload (no service restart required).

Anomaly Detection

Two-stage approach: Z-score analysis for univariate anomalies, isolation forest for multivariate pattern detection. Severity levels: HIGH (>0.9), MEDIUM (0.7-0.9), LOW (<0.7).

Kafka Topics

Input: mfs.txn.enriched | Output: mfs.alerts.txn

Infrastructure

Deployed on mfs-txn-mon-pod-01 under svc-txn-monitor. Alert data persisted to mfs_fraud_db.alerts table. Consumer group: mfs-txn-monitor-cg.

Related

EPC-202 (Epic), FRD-200 (Feature), FRD-201 (Velocity), FRD-202 (Anomaly), INC0080202 (Kafka lag issue)

Fraud Model Training Pipeline

End-to-end ML pipeline for training, evaluating, and deploying fraud detection models.

Pipeline Stages

  1. Data Extraction: Pull labeled transaction data from mfs_fraud_db.fraud_transactions on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal. Uses 6-month sliding window.
  2. Feature Engineering: Compute 47 features including velocity aggregates, merchant category embeddings, device fingerprint hashes, and geolocation risk scores.
  3. Model Training: XGBoost with Optuna hyperparameter optimization. Target: AUC-ROC > 0.96, false positive rate < 2%.
  4. Model Evaluation: Held-out test set evaluation plus shadow mode comparison against production model.
  5. Model Export: ONNX format for cross-platform serving compatibility.
  6. Registry: Model metadata, metrics, and artifacts stored in MLflow. Version tracked in mfs_fraud_db.model_registry.

A/B Testing

New models deployed with configurable traffic split (e.g., 90/10 production/candidate). Automated rollback if candidate model false positive rate exceeds production baseline by >0.5%.

Related

FRD-101 (Story), FRD-111 (Model Training Task), FRD-103 (A/B Testing), MR !601

Incident Runbook: Fraud Engine False Positive Spikes

This runbook covers diagnosis and remediation when the fraud scoring engine false positive rate exceeds the 2% SLA threshold.

Detection

Datadog monitor 'Fraud False Positive Rate' fires when FP rate > 2% over 5-minute window. Alert routed to #fraud-oncall Slack channel and PagerDuty.

Immediate Triage

  1. Check Grafana dashboard 'Fraud Engine SLOs' for score distribution shift
  2. Verify feature extraction freshness on mfs-fraud-pod-01: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl localhost:8080/health/features
  3. Check model version in production: kubectl exec -n mfs-prod mfs-fraud-pod-01 -- curl localhost:8080/model/version
  4. Review mfs_fraud_db reference table timestamps for staleness

Common Root Causes

CauseIndicatorFix
Stale feature reference datamerchant_risk table last_updated > 24h agoRun feature refresh job; see INC0080201
Model/feature version mismatchModel trained on feature set v(N) but serving v(N-1)Align feature pipeline version with model training config
Training data driftScore distribution diverges from training baselineRetrain model with recent data; trigger FRD-111 pipeline

Rollback

If false positive rate does not recover within 30 minutes: roll back to previous model version via svc-fraud-engine config: kubectl set env deployment/fraud-engine -n mfs-prod MODEL_VERSION=v1

Post-Incident

File ServiceNow incident. Update this runbook. Review in weekly fraud ops meeting.
